data.plain: The content hash records which bytes or rows were used; the provenance label records where they may go and how strongly they may be claimed. A piece of data needs both before it is fully routed.

analogy.boundary: The two-tag picture covers only the need for both at once; a fully tagged sample can still be the wrong sample.

maps.analogy: the label naming the patient and the draw
maps.doctrine: the recorded inputs the value was built from

maps.analogy: the handling tag stating what the sample may be tested for
maps.doctrine: the origin class and usage limit

maps.analogy: a tube with only one tag is set aside
maps.doctrine: a value missing either record is not fully described

analogy.text: A blood sample needs a label saying which patient and which draw it came from, and a handling tag saying what it may be tested for. A tube with only one of the two is set aside.

reader.counterexample: A reused result record has a clean origin label and no content hash, so it keeps being trusted after the source it was built from has changed.
reader.does_not_prove: Carrying both records shows a value is fully described, and says nothing about whether the value is correct.

example.text: The source-import protocol brings public material in with a manifest and a hash for each file, so the imported copy carries both the hash that detects source changes and the origin label that limits where it may go.

reader.governs: Values that are reused or that cross from one part of the system to another.
reader.plain: Every piece of data needs two tags at once, one saying exactly which inputs it was built from and one saying where it may go and how strongly it can be claimed. If either tag is missing, the data is not ready to use.
reader.potential_misread: That one good label is enough, when knowing the source says nothing about where a value may travel and a usage tag means little without the inputs.
reader.refuses: Treating a value as fully described when it records only its inputs or only its origin.
reader.requires: A recorded input hash that forces a recompute when it no longer matches, and an origin class with a usage limit carried across every boundary, both on the same value.
reader.why_it_matters: Data cannot be trusted on half a paper trail, where you know what it is but not where it may go, or the reverse.
